predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: the Louisiana territory that 'Spain had ceded ... back to France' in the (secret) Third Treaty of San Ildefonso, 1800

successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: the Louisiana Purchase, 'nominally' 828,000 sq mi (2,140,000 km2); New Orleans turned over 20 December 1803, Upper Louisiana at St.

ledger.x: 1800: Spain cedes Louisiana back to France in the secret Third Treaty of San Ildefonso.
1800: Upper Louisiana stays Spanish-run too; it passes 'from Spain to France' only on 9 March 1804 (Three Flags Day).
30 November 1803: Spain hands Louisiana to France at the Plaza de Armas (Jackson Square), New Orleans, 'ending Spanish administration'.
20 December 1803: France turns New Orleans over to the United States.
9 March 1804: 'Upper Louisiana passed from Spain to France' at St.
10 March 1804: Upper Louisiana passes from France to the United States at St.
1804: the last French Louisiana land goes to the United States.

wars.name: Haitian Revolution
wars.outcome: French defeat: General Leclerc's expedition (December 1801) 'faltered amid resistance and disease', France withdrew its 7,000 surviving troops in November 1803, gave up its Western Hemisphere ambitions and sold Louisiana.

certainty.note: The Louisiana boundaries were disputed: Spain held the western limit to the Mississippi's west bank and New Orleans/St.
